PARSE_XML returns the document element as a canonical JSON object with exactly four required non-null properties: name (exact element-name string), attributes (object of exact parsed attribute-name/string-value pairs), children (ordered array of its immediate element-node values), and content (ordered array of strings and immediate element-node values in source content order). Every child appears once in children and once as the same canonical value in content; this is duplicated value content, not a cyclic pointer or identity-based equality. Each nonempty ordinary text run between markup boundaries contributes one decoded string; each nonempty CDATA body contributes one literal string. Empty runs are omitted, comments contribute no entry, adjacent strings separated by comment/CDATA boundaries are not coalesced, and entity references within a text run are decoded into that one string. Outside-root whitespace and the declaration are not represented. Attribute order has no canonical-equality significance; child/content array order and text-run segmentation do. Thus differently ordered attributes with equal values compare equal, while mixed text/child content remains observable in exact document order. XML name/attribute/character normalization is precisely the parsing rule above, not namespace inference.

These canonical node values may be consumed by canonical equality, UNIQUE, ASSERT_SET_EQUAL and SELECT_JSON_PATH without opaque host-object behavior. For JSON-path traversal their object keys, including attributes, use §34.1 key order; XML traversal uses children/content source order. SELECT_XML requires a parsed node value from PARSE_XML or a node selected from that parsed value in the same execution; a lookalike authored JSON object does not acquire XML-node provenance. Provenance does not affect canonical equality. Its input is one node, not an implicitly unwrapped array; extraction from an element-result array is explicit through SELECT_JSON_PATH.

Regex uses a restricted, safe, JavaScript-compatible subset with enforced limits.
Regex cannot become an uncontrolled denial-of-service surface.

The current registry is closed-loop-regex/1. It MUST support at least: literal characters; `.`; character classes with ranges and negation; `\d`, `\D`, `\w`, `\W`, `\s`, and `\S`; anchors `^` and `$`; alternation; capturing and non-capturing groups; and greedy and lazy `*`, `+`, `?`, `{m}`, `{m,}`, and `{m,n}` quantifiers. Backreferences, lookaround assertions, Unicode property escapes, and every construct outside the registered subset are prohibited in version 1.

23.3 External-action risk contract

Every external, human, tool, system, physical, publication, filing, purchase, security, or production action is classified before package generation as one or more of:
READ_ONLY, REVERSIBLE, DESTRUCTIVE, IRREVERSIBLE, COST_INCURRING, THIRD_PARTY_AFFECTING, SECURITY_TESTING, PHYSICAL_HAZARD, or UNKNOWN.

The action contract records exact target, scope, expected effect, reversibility, maximum cost where applicable, legal or authority dependency where applicable, containment, rollback or stop condition, responsible actor, and required authorization. READ_ONLY or demonstrably safe REVERSIBLE actions may proceed under the normal stage authority. Any other class requires a current purpose- and target-bound HUMAN_DECISION before execution. UNKNOWN blocks. A test or prompt may never authorize action beyond the recorded target and risk scope.

Negative, adversarial, destructive, or security tests use isolated disposable state or an explicitly authorized bounded external sandbox. Canonical user projects and third-party systems are not mutation targets merely because a test requires an invalid state.

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

A failure or regression test is executed only when its target exists and its current EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE has been reached. Its REQUIRED_BY_STAGE may not precede target availability. A not-yet-due test remains registered and visible as future work but does not falsely block a prior convergence stage.

Every negative, mutation, adversarial, storage-failure, parser-hostility, and deliberately invalid fixture executes against isolated disposable state: a test-only project clone, test-only IndexedDB namespace, immutable read-only artifact copy, isolated worker input, or explicitly authorized external sandbox. The suite must prove that no fixture mutated a canonical user project or an unauthorized third-party target. Canonical user projects and third-party systems are never mutation targets unless the exact action is separately authorized and safely bounded.

Every stage operation that can produce a DATA_PROPOSAL declares exactly one acceptance mode in the STAGE_OPERATION_REGISTRY:
- HUMAN_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED: the validated pending proposal commits only after explicit operator acceptance through REVIEW_PROPOSAL or REVIEW_FILE_RESPONSE_PROPOSAL;
- VALIDATED_AUTO_COMMIT: the validated proposal commits without operator review.

HUMAN_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED is the default mode and is mandatory for Stage 01 COMPLETE and RECONCILE_INTAKE, wherever the proposal co-accepts a humanAuthorityCandidates confirmation under Section 14.10, and wherever the accepted result supersedes previously accepted current canonical records under a REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET policy. VALIDATED_AUTO_COMMIT is permitted only where the operation writes exclusively agent-owned fields into its own reserved target slot, carries no humanAuthorityCandidates, and embeds no genuine human-authority decision. Application commands never use proposal acceptance; they commit directly under Sections 22.4 and 36.12. The declared mode is closed and version-bound and cannot be altered by a response.

Reservation identity, target slot, prompt identity, package identity, challenge nonce, scope, and committed project revision are established in one application transaction as defined in Section 35.6. The package binds to that committed reservationRevision. Operational status transitions explicitly registered as non-scope-changing, such as marking a package exported or shared, do not invalidate their own package.

The reservation state machine is the closed set defined in Section 35.6: RESERVED → EXPORTED → RESPONSE_STAGED → ACCEPTED, with ORPHANED, RESUMED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, SUPERSEDED, and EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE as the only recovery or terminal states, as defined by the operation registry. Resume of an ORPHANED reservation preserves its original binding when still current.

Idempotency lookup occurs before stale-revision rejection only for an exact previously committed command identity and payload so an exact retry can return its original receipt. A different payload or command at a stale revision is rejected.

The controlling normative source is the exact UTF-8 file `specification/closed-loop-reliability-controlling-implementation-specification.txt` in the exact audited source commit. CI MUST generate `specification/closed-loop-specification-manifest.json` as a repository-only closed-loop-specification-manifest/1 after reading those exact bytes and MUST generate `specification/closed-loop-normative-requirements.json` as the corresponding normative-requirement manifest. That manifest records the source commit, repository path, artifact filename, byte length, SHA-256, section inventory, contract-profile identity, and the identity and digest of the normative-requirement manifest. The manifest and source commit together identify the exact specification used for implementation and acceptance; the specification does not contain a self-referential digest of itself.

The controlling runtime contract profile is closed-loop-completion-profile/1. Runtime project state, prompts, responses, packages, imports, exports, and receipts carry only the contract profile and the particular schema or registry identities required for their own operation. The specification text, its repository-only manifest, Section 0 implementation instructions, user-to-implementation-agent instructions, audits, and repair commentary are not runtime project data and MUST NOT be embedded in the application, generated prompts, execution packages, canonical records, or operator screens merely to establish conformance.

A closed-loop-project/3 object that lacks the current contract profile is legacy /3 data. It MUST be deterministically migrated with complete migration receipts or preserved as historical and non-gating. Schema-name equality alone does not establish current contract conformance.

2.2 Normative-requirement manifest

Repository governance MUST maintain one machine-readable closed-loop-normative-requirements/1 manifest generated from and reviewed against the controlling specification. It assigns a stable NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT_ID to every distinct normative requirement, prohibition, invariant, field contract, operation contract, negative case, regression obligation, deployment obligation, and definition-of-done metric. Each entry records the controlling text location, responsible implementation owner, schema or registry entry, deterministic and semantic test IDs, mutation-test IDs, required browser or physical-device proof, acceptance-report field, and current disposition.

This manifest is implementation and acceptance evidence outside runtime project state. It MUST NOT be injected into ordinary project prompts or carried by the application as project content. CI rejects missing, duplicated, untraced, or conflicting normative entries and rejects an acceptance claim when any current mandatory entry lacks the required implementation and proof relationships.

Manifest completeness is established under the same omission-challenge discipline this specification imposes on project content. One extractor drafts the manifest from the controlling text; an independent reviewer that did not receive the draft performs its own extraction or section-by-section coverage pass; a distinct reconciliation resolves every difference; and every specification section is either covered by entries or explicitly recorded as nonnormative with a reason. CI records the challenge and reconciliation evidence with the manifest digest. An unreconciled material disagreement, an uncovered section, or a missing challenge record blocks acceptance.

34.3 Registered normalizers and derivations

Every normalizer and application derivation has an immutable registry ID, version, implementation-owner file, canonical input contract, output contract, hash or build identity, and invalidation consequences. Every derived value records the exact derivation ID and source-record hashes. A changed normalizer or derivation invalidates affected current values and results unless an explicit compatibility migration proves byte- and semantic-equivalent output.

Every release-bearing derivation and normalizer is completely defined by this specification or by an explicitly named versioned normative algorithm. The semantics defined in Sections 14.6, 15, 16.1, 26, 29, 30, 31, 34.1, 34.2, and 36 control their registry entries, and an entry cannot deviate from them. A release-bearing derivation or normalizer whose semantics are not so defined is UNDEFINED_DERIVATION and blocks acceptance.

triggeringApprovedClauseReferences.controllingText: These clauses close result-bearing primitive/parser choices, not replace §§21.1–21.17. Named ports, DAG validation, immutable bindings, prohibited execution, limits and required identities remain as already specified. Unless expressly defaulted below, an omitted required argument is invalid; no coercion supplies it. The published registry must encode these rules exactly.

Remaining result-bearing argument/output closure: BYTE_COMPARE is exact length-and-byte equality of two byte inputs, with no ordering/operator default. ASSERT_MATCH asserts the same Boolean regex result as REGEX using actual/pattern/optional flags; ordered assertions use the exact ordering above. Each assertion yields only SATISFIED or VIOLATED on valid data, with other terminal dispositions propagated as D5 states. The optional message on assertions is a non-null string, absent by default, used only as diagnostic text and never to alter a result. SORT/UNIQUE require arrays and return arrays; MIN/MAX/SUM require arrays as stated. HASH_SHA256 requires bytes; REGEX requires string value/pattern; selectors require a string path and the defined structured value. Unknown optional arguments and implicit operand/binding selection are prohibited. Authoring shortcuts remain permitted only when they compile to the identical explicit §21.3 DAG and named ports. No extra primitive, alternate successful result type or undeclared default is authorized by registry publication. These additions close the result-bearing choices identified in the bounded argument/port omission comparison; the full generated registry still receives the independent §§2.2/14.5 review.

A structural node is counted once per occurrence/location/kind; a node's structural unit and its descendant content units are distinct. Detailed coverage requires a closed format mapping that is part of this named versioned normative algorithm or an explicitly identified versioned normative format mapping authorized under §34.3. ID_PAYLOAD = first 160 bits of SHA-256(
  closed-loop-canonical-json/1({
    "idVersion":"closed-loop-id/1",
    "familyNamespace":"<registered family namespace>",
    "jobNamespace":"<JOB_ID or registered global metadata namespace>",
    "commandId":"<application command ID>",
    "targetSlot":"<target slot or empty string>",
    "parentId":"<parent ID or empty string>",
    "allocationSequence":<safe integer>,
    "collisionCounter":<safe integer>
  })
)

ID_PAYLOAD is the first 20 digest bytes in SHA-256 output order. base32hex uses alphabet `0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv`, most-significant-bit first, lowercase, with no padding. CANONICAL_ID = <FAMILY_PREFIX> + "-" + base32hex(ID_PAYLOAD).

The application begins collisionCounter at 0 and increments it only when the generated ID already exists for a different allocation tuple. The collision check and any increment occur inside the same transaction. Exact command retry returns the original ID from the idempotency receipt and does not reserve a new sequence. Content equality alone never collapses separately authorized records. Clone remapping uses the clone JOB_ID namespace and records the complete source-to-clone mapping. Raw-input accounting MUST use one versioned RAW_UNITIZATION_VERSION — current value closed-loop-raw-units/1 — with deterministic media-specific unit rules. Text-message boundaries, structured text units, document pages and sections where mechanically available, archive members, embedded documents, native images and media, unsupported-format whole-file fallbacks, and source locations receive stable application-owned unit identities.

The unitization contract explicitly defines treatment of comments, annotations, tracked changes, metadata, embedded objects, inaccessible content, and unsupported formats. A supported subdivision cannot be replaced by one whole-file unit merely to make coverage vacuous. A material uncovered unit, broad exclusion, INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED material, material uncertainty, contradiction, or operator request triggers regardless of size. These limits are centralized, versioned, and acceptance-tested and may be lowered but not raised without a new contract-profile identity.

Every current /3 project carries CONTRACT_PROFILE_ID = closed-loop-completion-profile/1. A /3 project lacking that exact profile is pre-profile legacy data and cannot satisfy current gates. referenceSourceLocation.controllingText: Use the base C unit kinds STRUCTURAL_NODE, ARTIFACT_INVENTORY, PHYSICAL_SPAN and STRUCTURAL_TEXT_SPAN only; do not add canonical record families or a second unit-ID scheme. Every archive, member, metadata, extra and comment structural node uses occurrence P of the archive being mapped; child inventories/content and recursively mapped child archive nodes use P followed by i. Every ZIP structural unit's locator is ["closed-loop-raw-units-zip/1", locatorValue], where locatorValue is one of the exact ordered arrays below. All offsets and lengths are nonnegative safe integers measured in the parent archive's original bytes; an index is a zero-based safe integer. A node with verified source bytes has status ACCESSIBLE. Its C source-value hash is H(C({"nodeKind":k,"status":"ACCESSIBLE","value":v})); the outer binding hash uses the unchanged C input-version/occurrence/kind/locator/source-value preimage. Exact raw bytes below use lowercase hexadecimal, preserving every byte without character decoding. Metadata offsets/bytes belong to the archive, not to a reserialized ZIP.

resolvedSuccessorSourceRanges.controllingText: The unit universe is structural accounting. Retain the exact originating input and artifact bytes; no normalized projection replaces them or asserts inspection. Each unit binds the input version, supplied occurrence, exact structural location and source-value hash. Enumerate roots in their retained source occurrence order; within a structured value visit arrays in index order and object keys in unsigned Unicode-scalar order. A canonical mirror of the same originating field is visited only once, using the originating field; separately supplied equal values are separate occurrences.

For every supplied artifact occurrence, emit one inventory unit. Where exact bytes are valid UTF-8 and the text projection re-encodes to those exact bytes, also emit physical content units: scan left to right, treating CRLF as one terminator and otherwise CR, LF or form feed as a terminator; each unit contains the span through its terminator. Retain every nonempty span, including blank lines; emit a final unterminated span if present, but no zero-length trailing span. Coordinates start at page 1/line 1; form feed increments page and resets line to 1, other terminators increment line. BOM bytes, if present, remain part of the exact projection, not silently removed. This rule is accounting, not a claim that every UTF-8 artifact's media semantics have been parsed.

For a mechanically supported structured-media subdivision, emit one structural unit per exposed page, section, archive member, embedded document/object, comment, annotation, tracked change or metadata object, using its exact parent and source locator; traverse children in source order, breaking any absent source-order tie by unsigned Unicode-scalar locator order. Recurse into textual leaves using the physical-content rule and into child media using this rule. A structural node is counted once per occurrence/location/kind; a node's structural unit and its descendant content units are distinct. Preserve inaccessible exposed nodes as INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED; do not fabricate children. Detailed coverage requires a closed format mapping that is part of this named versioned normative algorithm or an explicitly identified versioned normative format mapping authorized under §34.3. Merely publishing an implementation descriptor does not authorize such semantics. The mapping must fix node kinds, source locators, ordering, exact canonical source values and child extraction. This insertion adds no format-specific adapter or mapping. A claim of supported detailed coverage without that normative mapping is blocked; genuinely unsupported formats retain the fallback below. A mechanically available subdivision cannot be suppressed or relabeled unsupported to avoid that blocker.

Subdivision is additive: an exact UTF-8 whole-file projection emits its physical spans even when a supported structured mapping also emits structural nodes and textual leaves. Whole-file spans, structural nodes and structural textual-leaf spans have distinct kinds and locators and are all counted; overlap in underlying bytes does not deduplicate these different accounting obligations. Each archive-member or embedded-file occurrence emits both its parent structural occurrence unit and its own child inventory unit, followed by its own supported content/subdivisions. A textual leaf is not a child file and gets no inventory unit. Repeated references to the same emitted unit still deduplicate under the rule below.

Source hashes and binding are closed as follows. C(x) means the exact UTF-8 bytes of §34.1 canonical JSON; H(b) means lowercase SHA-256 hexadecimal of exact bytes b. Source-value hash preimages by kind are:

- ARTIFACT_INVENTORY: C({"byteLength":n,"contentSha256":h}), where n is exact byte length and h=H(exact artifact bytes). If bytes are unavailable, both values are null; asserted length/digest remains source context, never substituted for observed bytes. The unit remains inaccessible/blocked, with its retained occurrence/locator binding.

- PHYSICAL_SPAN: the exact original byte span including its terminator, without canonical JSON wrapping. Its locator binds zero-based byte start and exclusive end plus the one-based page/line coordinates.

- STRUCTURAL_NODE: C({"nodeKind":k,"status":q,"value":v}), where k and v are the exact kind and canonical source value fixed by the authorized format mapping, and q is ACCESSIBLE or INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED. Inaccessible nodes have v=null; exact exposed parent/locator and k remain bound. No invented serialization of an adapter object is permitted.

- STRUCTURAL_TEXT_SPAN: exact UTF-8 bytes of the mapped exact textual leaf's physical span, including its terminator. The authorized mapping identifies the leaf and its exact extraction; no silent whitespace normalization is allowed.

Each unit's binding hash preimage is C({"algorithm":"closed-loop-raw-units/1","inputVersion":V,"occurrence":O,"kind":K,"locator":L,"sourceValueSha256":S}). V is the exact owning input-version identity string; O is the ordered zero-based safe-integer path of supplied root and, where applicable, child-member occurrence indices; K is exactly one of the seven uppercase kinds above; S is the corresponding source-value hash. L is an ordered locator array: human units use [originating JSON pointer, one-based physical line] or [originating JSON pointer] for whole strings/scalars; inventories use []; whole-file spans use [startByte,endByte,page,line]; structural nodes use [normative format mapping ID, exact mapping locator]; structural textual spans append [startByte,endByte,page,line] to their structural-leaf locator. Byte offsets for a structural textual leaf refer to its exact UTF-8 extraction. The source-value hash alone does not identify the occurrence: binding hash plus retained input/source supplies the exact type, location and occurrence. These accounting hashes/locators are not §34.2 canonical record IDs. Distinct roots are numbered in retained source occurrence order, including separately supplied identical roots; a canonical mirror does not receive a second root number.

Deduplicate only repeated accounting references to the same occurrence, kind, location and exact source-value hash. Never merge distinct supplied occurrences, even with identical hashes. Order and retained source identity determine stable accounting references; canonical record IDs still use §34.2. Count the entire resulting unit universe, including inventory, structural and inaccessible units, when applying the unchanged §6.5A limits. The raw-unit challenge condition is strictly greater than 500, not greater than or equal to 500; every other size-independent trigger remains effective.

referenceSourceLocation.controllingText: For every verified expanded child, apply the byte/claim recognition test above. A ZIP candidate is mapped recursively by this same mapping, in depth-first central-directory order, under the entire input-version mapping pass's shared cumulative safety counters and deadline. The expanded child becomes the next archive occurrence P; no new root identity, fresh budget or favorable parent result is substituted. Exact expanded bytes remain retained and bound even when their own ZIP structure is blocked. A ZIP-based document can expose these ZIP members without thereby claiming semantic Office/XML/PDF parsing. A child that is not a ZIP candidate still receives its inventory and applicable exact UTF-8 physical spans under C; this addendum invents no other media mapping.

resolvedSuccessorSourceRanges.controllingText: For every supplied artifact occurrence, emit one inventory unit. Where exact bytes are valid UTF-8 and the text projection re-encodes to those exact bytes, also emit physical content units: scan left to right, treating CRLF as one terminator and otherwise CR, LF or form feed as a terminator; each unit contains the span through its terminator. Retain every nonempty span, including blank lines; emit a final unterminated span if present, but no zero-length trailing span. Coordinates start at page 1/line 1; form feed increments page and resets line to 1, other terminators increment line. BOM bytes, if present, remain part of the exact projection, not silently removed. This rule is accounting, not a claim that every UTF-8 artifact's media semantics have been parsed.

Subdivision is additive: an exact UTF-8 whole-file projection emits its physical spans even when a supported structured mapping also emits structural nodes and textual leaves. Whole-file spans, structural nodes and structural textual-leaf spans have distinct kinds and locators and are all counted; overlap in underlying bytes does not deduplicate these different accounting obligations. Each archive-member or embedded-file occurrence emits both its parent structural occurrence unit and its own child inventory unit, followed by its own supported content/subdivisions. A textual leaf is not a child file and gets no inventory unit. Repeated references to the same emitted unit still deduplicate under the rule below.

- ARTIFACT_INVENTORY: C({"byteLength":n,"contentSha256":h}), where n is exact byte length and h=H(exact artifact bytes). If bytes are unavailable, both values are null; asserted length/digest remains source context, never substituted for observed bytes. The unit remains inaccessible/blocked, with its retained occurrence/locator binding.

- PHYSICAL_SPAN: the exact original byte span including its terminator, without canonical JSON wrapping. Its locator binds zero-based byte start and exclusive end plus the one-based page/line coordinates.

Each unit's binding hash preimage is C({"algorithm":"closed-loop-raw-units/1","inputVersion":V,"occurrence":O,"kind":K,"locator":L,"sourceValueSha256":S}). V is the exact owning input-version identity string; O is the ordered zero-based safe-integer path of supplied root and, where applicable, child-member occurrence indices; K is exactly one of the seven uppercase kinds above; S is the corresponding source-value hash. L is an ordered locator array: human units use [originating JSON pointer, one-based physical line] or [originating JSON pointer] for whole strings/scalars; inventories use []; whole-file spans use [startByte,endByte,page,line]; structural nodes use [normative format mapping ID, exact mapping locator]; structural textual spans append [startByte,endByte,page,line] to their structural-leaf locator. Byte offsets for a structural textual leaf refer to its exact UTF-8 extraction. The source-value hash alone does not identify the occurrence: binding hash plus retained input/source supplies the exact type, location and occurrence. These accounting hashes/locators are not §34.2 canonical record IDs. Distinct roots are numbered in retained source occurrence order, including separately supplied identical roots; a canonical mirror does not receive a second root number.

Apply the same recognition test to each supplied root and each verified expanded child. A byte candidate exists if the first four bytes are a ZIP local-header, EOCD, ZIP64 EOCD or ZIP64-locator signature (respectively hexadecimal 504b0304, 504b0506, 504b0606, 504b0607), or if the EOCD signature 504b0506 occurs anywhere in the last min(byteLength,65557) bytes. Also attempt validation when a supplied filename ends with .zip under ASCII case-insensitive comparison, or the supplied media type, before a semicolon and after ASCII whitespace trim/case-fold, is application/zip or application/x-zip-compressed. Names and media types can require an attempt but cannot suppress a byte candidate or establish success. A random signature or claimed filename can never create successful ZIP coverage: the complete retained structural, boundary, path and integrity checks decide that. Missing bytes retain an unavailable inventory/blocker; they do not establish absence of ZIP structure. Noncandidate bytes without a ZIP claim do not receive ZIP nodes through speculation; C's other available accounting rules remain applicable.

Use a centralized, versioned intake profile closed-loop-raw-units-zip-limits/1. Its bounds are: 27 cumulative central-directory entries across the entire selected input-version archive-mapping pass, including every supplied root and recursively decoded child; 67108864 bytes per expanded member; 70254592 cumulative reserved-or-produced expanded bytes; 140509184 cumulative archive bytes submitted to decoding (count a nested archive again when it is submitted); compression ratio at most 1100 per member; filename byte length at most 65535; canonical path depth at most 128; maximum archive nesting level 27 with the supplied archive at level 1; and one cumulative elapsed-worker deadline of 600000 ms for that entire input-version archive-mapping pass. The entry budget is charged on exposure before expansion, including unsupported/blocked entries; the maximum depth cannot bypass that budget. Expansion and byte accounting are checked before allocation and incrementally, against both declared and actual lengths; declared metadata never substitutes for verified bytes. The expansion safety counter reserves each declared output length before allocation; actual production within that reservation does not charge the same byte twice, while any additional produced byte must first fit and consume remaining budget. Every produced/reserved byte remains charged even if later CRC, validation or decoding fails; no refund, reset or retry can escape the pass-wide ceiling. It includes every child occurrence at every depth, including a nested archive's bytes as its parent's output and its own children separately. This work-safety counter is distinct from the semantic aggregate-byte review sum, which includes only actually verified retained child bytes. The archive-byte sum counts each archive occurrence once when submitted to decoding. The same original per-archive structural and byte checks remain; a bound can stop processing earlier, never authorize weaker checking. These ceilings reuse the current default decoder's 27 entries, 64 MiB file bound, 64 MiB + 1 MiB response + 2 MiB manifest total, twice-total archive bound, ratio/name/path/work bounds; the intake profile assigns those generic ceilings without granting any response.json/manifest.json role or larger filename-specific allowance. Transport recursiveExpansion=false and maxNestingDepth=0 remain response-transport rules, not intake accounting rules. A lower already-applicable storage/worker bound still stops work and remains explicitly blocked; it must not silently change this profile or yield favorable completeness. The exact profile-hash preimage is C({"version":"closed-loop-raw-units-zip-limits/1","scope":"INPUT_VERSION_PASS","maxEntries":27,"maxEntryBytes":67108864,"maxExpandedBytes":70254592,"maxArchiveBytes":140509184,"maxCompressionRatio":1100,"maxFilenameBytes":65535,"maxPathDepth":128,"maxNestingDepth":27,"workerTimeoutMs":600000}); its SHA-256 is the profile hash. The retained unitization derivation binds the owning input version, mapping ID, this exact profile ID/hash, actual counters and completion/blocker status; changed profile or source invalidates reuse under the existing derivation rules. Repeated equal roots and members are charged separately. Any future profile change follows existing versioning and acceptance requirements.

Let P be the parent archive's C occurrence path, already bound to the owning input version. Number central-directory entries from zero in their exact central-directory order, not local-file-offset order, canonical-filename order or extraction completion order. The child occurrence for entry i is P followed by i. Different supplied archives and different nested occurrences remain distinct even when bytes or names are equal. Local/central identity validation is still required; choosing central-directory order for accounting does not weaken it.

5. One child ARTIFACT_INVENTORY with occurrence P followed by i and inventory locator [], binding the actual expanded byte length and H(expanded bytes) by C. Then emit that child's exact verified UTF-8 physical spans when C permits them, using offsets in the expanded child bytes, and apply the recursive rule below before proceeding to entry i+1. A recursively mapped child archive uses this already-emitted inventory and physical spans without emitting them a second time. The ZIP_MEMBER structural node and child inventory are different accounting obligations and both count. Metadata/comment nodes are not child files and do not receive inventory units. This mapping creates no semantic XML/JSON/CSV/Office/PDF section or annotation units from a member's contents; plain supported UTF-8 spans do not claim such parsing or inspection.

When a depth, entry, byte, ratio, path, name, worker or work bound actually stops a recognized child, retain that child's already exposed member occurrence, inventory and available exact bytes, mark its unresolved subdivision INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED with the precise cause, and stop the affected expansion safely. It is neither a successful opaque fallback nor proof that children do not exist. Never reset counters for nested ZIPs, invoke unbounded recursive decompression, fabricate descendants, or treat unknown remaining units as zero. A separately supplied copy is a separate root occurrence with its own identity and is charged again to the same input-version pass counters; equality of bytes does not merge it or reset the budget.

resolvedBaseSourceRanges.controllingText:
Every artifact preserves rawFilename and has a safe displayFilename and canonicalPath under closed-loop-filename/1. Canonical comparison uses Unicode 15.1.0 NFC, case-sensitive identity, and separately checked Unicode 15.1.0 default-case-fold and registered platform-risk collision keys. Absolute paths, drive prefixes, NUL, control characters, empty segments, `.` and `..`, duplicate canonical paths, case-fold collisions, extraction-target collisions, and supported confusable collisions are rejected. An unauthorized rename never matches solely because bytes are equal.

File extension and browser MIME type are claims. Format-dependent work records the authorized parser or adapter and detected interpretation. A materially ambiguous polyglot is BLOCKED unless one interpretation is explicitly authorized and every alternate interpretation is harmless under the operation.

Archive intake and export fail closed on traversal, absolute paths, duplicate or colliding paths, symlinks, hard links, device entries, unsupported special files, unsupported or encrypted members outside a registered encrypted contract, unsupported compression, excessive nesting, entry count, per-entry size, total compressed or expanded size, compression ratio, path depth, filename length, Unicode ambiguity, manifest mismatch, unmanifested extra members, missing members, or modified bytes. Expansion occurs only in an isolated bounded parser path and never makes content executable or prompt-visible by itself.

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

13.1 Contract-profile migration

Every current /3 project carries CONTRACT_PROFILE_ID = closed-loop-completion-profile/1. A /3 project lacking that exact profile is pre-profile legacy data and cannot satisfy current gates. Migration either deterministically creates every required current-profile record and field with auditable receipts and valid provenance or preserves the project as historical and non-gating. Merely setting CONTRACT_PROFILE_ID without satisfying the profile validator is rejected.

Migration defaults cannot fabricate semantic review, human authority, execution, evidence, freshness, independence, backup custody, mobile acceptance, or delivery. Any such missing release-bearing fact remains UNKNOWN or incomplete. Contract-profile migration is idempotent and is covered by invalid legacy fixtures.

13.2 Registry-version migration

Every persisted reference to a field contract, stage operation, scope matrix, Test IR language or operation registry, parser or selector registry, canonicalization contract, ID contract, filename contract, date/time contract, handoff container, normalizer, or derivation is version-bound. Import or migration must either prove compatibility under an explicit migration rule or invalidate and regenerate the affected current work. Equal high-level schema names do not imply registry compatibility.

Any operation, argument, dataflow, output, parser, selector, regex, numeric, or error-semantic change creates a new language or registry identity. An affected test or result under an earlier identity becomes stale and cannot satisfy a current proof obligation until explicitly migrated and reverified. Two runtimes MUST NOT claim the same current language identity while accepting materially different operations or semantics.

Every normalizer and application derivation has an immutable registry ID, version, implementation-owner file, canonical input contract, output contract, hash or build identity, and invalidation consequences. Every derived value records the exact derivation ID and source-record hashes. A changed normalizer or derivation invalidates affected current values and results unless an explicit compatibility migration proves byte- and semantic-equivalent output.

Every release-bearing derivation and normalizer is completely defined by this specification or by an explicitly named versioned normative algorithm. The semantics defined in Sections 14.6, 15, 16.1, 26, 29, 30, 31, 34.1, 34.2, and 36 control their registry entries, and an entry cannot deviate from them. A release-bearing derivation or normalizer whose semantics are not so defined is UNDEFINED_DERIVATION and blocks acceptance.

21. Closed Loop Test IR

21.1 Purpose

An AI verification architect designs the test.
The application owns the test language, validates the test, and executes every faithfully expressible mechanical test.
The AI acts as a compiler targeting an application-owned declarative language.
The AI does not invent runtime semantics.

21.2 Canonical test additions

The canonical tests record adds:

EXECUTABLE_KIND
- Producer: AGENT
- Allowed values: NONE, TEST_IR

EXECUTABLE_SPEC_VERSION
- Producer: APPLICATION
- Accepted current value: closed-loop-test-spec/1

EXECUTABLE_SPEC
- Producer: AGENT
- Canonical normalized composable Test IR

EXECUTABLE_INPUT_BINDINGS
- Producer: AGENT
- Application-validated artifact and immutable canonical bindings

Canonical Test IR hash
- Producer: APPLICATION
- Calculated from normalized executable specification

A giant high-level taxonomy of project-specific test types must not coexist as a second runtime language.
Authoring shortcuts may exist only when they compile to the exact canonical primitive IR before acceptance.

21.3 Canonical structure and dataflow

Test IR is a topologically ordered directed acyclic graph. Every step has a unique application-validated stepId, one registered op, and an explicit inputs object. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. Hidden accumulators, implicit stacks, ambient project state, ambient current values, operand-by-position rules, and implementation-dependent input selection are prohibited.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.

21.4 Required primitives

Version 1 supports:
- LOAD_ARTIFACT
- READ_BYTES
- DECODE_UTF8
- PARSE_JSON
- PARSE_CSV
- PARSE_XML
- SELECT_JSON_PATH
- SELECT_XML
- COUNT
- SUM
- MIN
- MAX
- SORT
- UNIQUE
- HASH_SHA256
- REGEX
- COMPARE
- ASSERT_EQ
- ASSERT_GT
- ASSERT_GTE
- ASSERT_LT
- ASSERT_LTE
- ASSERT_MATCH
- ASSERT_CONTAINS
- ASSERT_NOT_CONTAINS
- ASSERT_SET_EQUAL
- BYTE_COMPARE

Additional primitives may be added only when a demonstrated acceptance case cannot be faithfully represented using the existing set.

21.5 Prohibited runtime behavior

Version 1 prohibits:
- arbitrary JavaScript;
- arbitrary Python;
- shell commands;
- dynamic imports;
- eval;
- Function;
- arbitrary network access;
- unrestricted project-state access;
- user-provided executable source;
- agent-provided executable source;
- a CUSTOM_PIPELINE that means unregistered code.

Any future "custom pipeline" may mean only a composition of registered declarative primitives.

21.6 Restricted selectors

SELECT_JSON_PATH and SELECT_XML use restricted application-owned selector contracts.
The application cannot claim complete third-party JSONPath or XPath semantics unless a specific implementation is explicitly adopted, versioned, and regression-tested.
Unknown or unsupported selector syntax fails Stage 06 ingestion.

The current registries are closed-loop-json-selector/1 and closed-loop-xml-selector/1. closed-loop-json-selector/1 MUST support at least: the root `$`; child access by identifier name and by single-quoted bracket name; nonnegative array index; and the wildcard `*` over object values and array elements. Selection order is document order. Recursive descent, filters, unions, slices, and script expressions are excluded from version 1. closed-loop-xml-selector/1 MUST support at least: absolute child-element paths from the document root; the element wildcard `*`; 1-based positional index predicates; attribute access `@name`; and `text()` value extraction. All other axes, predicates, and functions are excluded from version 1. A proposition that cannot be faithfully expressed within these registered subsets is not natively representable and routes externally.

21.7 CSV contract

CSV parsing explicitly binds:
- delimiter;
- header presence;
- quoting behavior;
- newline handling;
- UTF-8 encoding assumption.

Ambiguous parser defaults cannot control verification.

PARSE_CSV outputs one normalized JSON value — an array of row arrays, or an array of objects keyed by exact header names when header presence is declared — and that output is addressed with SELECT_JSON_PATH; no separate CSV selector exists in version 1.

21.8 Text encoding

Version 1 supports UTF-8.
Unsupported encodings route to an external executor or remain blocked.

21.9 Regex

Regex uses a restricted, safe, JavaScript-compatible subset with enforced limits.
Regex cannot become an uncontrolled denial-of-service surface.

The current registry is closed-loop-regex/1. It MUST support at least: literal characters; `.`; character classes with ranges and negation; `\d`, `\D`, `\w`, `\W`, `\s`, and `\S`; anchors `^` and `$`; alternation; capturing and non-capturing groups; and greedy and lazy `*`, `+`, `?`, `{m}`, `{m,}`, and `{m,n}` quantifiers. Backreferences, lookaround assertions, Unicode property escapes, and every construct outside the registered subset are prohibited in version 1.

21.10 Numeric semantics

- Integer operations remain exact.
- Precision-sensitive decimal equality cannot silently use binary floating-point equality.
- Approximate comparisons require explicit absolute tolerance, relative tolerance, or both.
- Exact decimal-string interpretation may be used.
- Unsupported precision requirements route externally rather than being silently approximated.

21.11 Inputs

A Test IR specification may:
- consume one artifact;
- consume multiple artifacts;
- compare two artifacts byte-for-byte;
- read explicit application-selected immutable canonical bindings;
- use literal expected values;
- use hash-bound current canonical values selected by the application.

It cannot access unrestricted project state.

21.12 Format adapters

PDF, DOCX, XLSX, SVG, DXF, STL, G-code, image, archive, and other specialized parsers are adapters.
They are not project-subject modules.
An unsupported format cannot be represented as natively executable.

21.13 JSON Schema

Native JSON Schema support is required only when implemented deterministically without arbitrary execution.
Unsupported JSON Schema semantics route externally.

21.14 Resource limits

Centralized hard limits cover:
- total input bytes;
- decompressed bytes;
- IR step count;
- selector depth;
- parsed structure depth;
- collection size;
- regex pattern size;
- regex input size;
- worker execution duration;
- archive expansion where applicable.

The implementation selects explicit constants, centralizes them, documents them, and regression-tests every boundary.
Limits must not be scattered throughout the code.

21.15 Execution dispositions

- Required material unavailable before execution → BLOCKED
- Execution starts but exceeds a runtime limit → EXECUTION_FAILED
- Execution finishes but cannot establish the proposition → UNDETERMINED
- Assertion establishes compliance → SATISFIED
- Assertion establishes noncompliance → VIOLATED

21.16 Test IR language and registry identity

Every Test IR specification and every result binds:
- TEST_IR_LANGUAGE_VERSION;
- OPERATION_REGISTRY_VERSION;
- OPERATION_REGISTRY_SHA256;
- JSON_SELECTOR_REGISTRY_VERSION and digest when used;
- XML_SELECTOR_REGISTRY_VERSION and digest when used;
- REGEX_REGISTRY_VERSION and digest when used;
- parser registry identities used by the execution.

Any operation, argument, dataflow, output, parser, selector, regex, numeric, or error-semantic change creates a new language or registry identity. An affected test or result under an earlier identity becomes stale and cannot satisfy a current proof obligation until explicitly migrated and reverified. Two runtimes MUST NOT claim the same current language identity while accepting materially different operations or semantics.

21.17 Verification timing fields

Every canonical test declares VERIFICATION_PHASE, EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE, REQUIRED_BY_STAGE, PER_RUN_REQUIRED, FINAL_PRODUCT_REQUIRED, DELIVERY_REQUIRED, and TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION. The application validates these values against the test role and proof obligation and derives when execution is due.

- consume multiple artifacts;
- compare two artifacts byte-for-byte;

- use literal expected values;

PDF, DOCX, XLSX, SVG, DXF, STL, G-code, image, archive, and other specialized parsers are adapters.

Native JSON Schema support is required only when implemented deterministically without arbitrary execution.
Unsupported JSON Schema semantics route externally.

- decompressed bytes;
- IR step count;
- selector depth;
- parsed structure depth;
- collection size;
- regex pattern size;

- worker execution duration;

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

29.15 Normative classification, controlled exceptions, severity, and materiality

Requirement classification is MANDATORY, CONDITIONAL, OPTIONAL, or UNKNOWN. Any classification that reduces a possible mandatory obligation requires independent review. UNKNOWN blocks wherever the item could be mandatory. A source-mandated or nonwaivable obligation cannot be weakened by an agent or unsupported human exception.

A controlled exception never converts a violated proposition into SATISFIED. It is either an authorized scope change creating new input and requirements versions, an authoritative waiver represented as a new governing obligation with its own proposition and evidence, or a blocker where authority is insufficient. Every exception records authority, reason, scope, effective period, affected propositions, independent challenge when obligations are reduced, and downstream invalidation.

Defect severity is CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR, or UNKNOWN. Severity is semantic and provenance-bound, but no severity label can override proposition truth. Sufficient refutation of an applicable mandatory proposition blocks release regardless of severity. UNKNOWN severity blocks severity-dependent routing.

Materiality is MATERIAL, NONMATERIAL, or UNKNOWN. MATERIAL means the item could change the truth value, applicability, proof admissibility, evidence sufficiency, identity, due state, dependency closure, gate result, authorization, or delivery status of at least one current release-bearing proposition or action. NONMATERIAL requires affirmative reasoning that the item cannot alter any current proposition, proof obligation, artifact identity, dependency, gate, release eligibility, delivery scope, or delivery state. UNKNOWN is treated as MATERIAL for exclusion and blocking. Every materiality determination that excludes content, reduces required work, or downgrades an obligation is recorded as a materialityReviews record; where it reduces a possible obligation it requires independent review under Section 26.5.

Stage 10 — FREEZE THE TEST CANDIDATE
Role: Configuration-control reviewer
Operations: FREEZE
Visible explanation: Select the exact files that make up this candidate.
The human selects components through the RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION command; FREEZE consumes and references that current decision.
The application assigns identities, freezes actual bytes and versions, calculates hashes, and prevents in-place mutation.
Completion: All required components are present and every run will receive the exact same frozen package.

Stage 13 — COMPARE THE TEN EXECUTIONS
Role: Cross-run comparison analyst
Operations: COMPARE
The prompt compares all ten current verified runs requirement by requirement.
The application calculates aggregate and stability values.
Completion: Every due PER_RUN_REQUIRED mandatory proposition has one comparison covering all ten current runs under its frozen expected-variance contract. Allowed variance is recorded; prohibited variance has a defect; UNKNOWN variance remains blocked.

ITERATION_ID, COMPARISON_VERSION, REQUIREMENT_COMPARISON_RECORDS, REQUIREMENTS_SATISFIED_BY_ALL_TEN, REQUIREMENTS_WITH_AT_LEAST_ONE_VIOLATION, REQUIREMENTS_WITH_AT_LEAST_ONE_UNDETERMINED, CORRECTNESS_AFFECTING_DISAGREEMENTS, PROHIBITED_OUTPUT_VARIANCES, INCONCLUSIVE_TESTS, REPEATED_FAILURE_GROUPS, UNIQUE_FAILURES, STAGE_DECISION, DECISION_EVIDENCE.

Stage 18 — CONTINUE UNTIL CONVERGENCE
Role: Convergence reviewer
Operations: COMPLETE
The application calculates convergence from the latest completed current iteration.
Completion: Every current applicable PREPRODUCT_ITERATION obligation due by Stage 18 is SATISFIED; required per-run verification and applicable regression coverage equal 1.0; every due blocking defect, mandatory unknown, contradiction, ambiguity, and unexplained variance count is zero simultaneously. Later-phase product, representation, delivery, evidence, registry, and terminal obligations remain scheduled and are not falsely treated as due.

ITERATION_ID, METRICS_VERSION, TOTAL_MANDATORY_REQUIREMENTS, MANDATORY_REQUIREMENTS_WITH_COMPLETE_SPECIFICATION_AND_APPLICABILITY, MANDATORY_REQUIREMENT_COVERAGE, MANDATORY_REQUIREMENTS_WITH_AFFIRMATIVE_APPLICABLE_VERIFICATION, MANDATORY_VERIFICATION_COVERAGE, TOTAL_STILL_APPLICABLE_REGRESSION_TESTS, SUCCESSFUL_REGRESSION_TESTS, REGRESSION_TEST_SUCCESS, CRITICAL_DEFECTS, MAJOR_DEFECTS, MANDATORY_UNRESOLVED_UNKNOWNS, KNOWN_CORRECTNESS_AFFECTING_CONTRADICTIONS, KNOWN_CORRECTNESS_AFFECTING_AMBIGUITIES, UNEXPLAINED_CORRECTNESS_AFFECTING_EXECUTION_VARIANCE, ALL_CONDITIONS_SIMULTANEOUSLY_TRUE, FAILED_CONDITIONS, RETURN_STAGE_FOR_EACH_FAILURE, STAGE_DECISION, DECISION_EVIDENCE.

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. 29.15 Normative classification, controlled exceptions, severity, and materiality

Requirement classification is MANDATORY, CONDITIONAL, OPTIONAL, or UNKNOWN. Any classification that reduces a possible mandatory obligation requires independent review. UNKNOWN blocks wherever the item could be mandatory. A source-mandated or nonwaivable obligation cannot be weakened by an agent or unsupported human exception.

A controlled exception never converts a violated proposition into SATISFIED. It is either an authorized scope change creating new input and requirements versions, an authoritative waiver represented as a new governing obligation with its own proposition and evidence, or a blocker where authority is insufficient. Sufficient refutation of an applicable mandatory proposition blocks release regardless of severity. UNKNOWN severity blocks severity-dependent routing.

Materiality is MATERIAL, NONMATERIAL, or UNKNOWN. MATERIAL means the item could change the truth value, applicability, proof admissibility, evidence sufficiency, identity, due state, dependency closure, gate result, authorization, or delivery status of at least one current release-bearing proposition or action. NONMATERIAL requires affirmative reasoning that the item cannot alter any current proposition, proof obligation, artifact identity, dependency, gate, release eligibility, delivery scope, or delivery state. UNKNOWN is treated as MATERIAL for exclusion and blocking. Every materiality determination that excludes content, reduces required work, or downgrades an obligation is recorded as a materialityReviews record; where it reduces a possible obligation it requires independent review under Section 26.5.

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION is a required, non-null closed canonical object with exactly one required non-null property PROOF_EXPRESSION_ID, a canonical proofExpressions ID string. It is one immutable owning-record-to-proofExpressions relationship, with no default. Its producer, scope, writable operation and invalidation owner follow the owning record's existing proposal/acceptance contract; the APPLICATION alone resolves and installs the canonical relationship. It is stored on that existing record, not in a new family.

The authored form is records.<owning family>[i].fields.TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION = {"PROOF_EXPRESSION_ID": <reference>}. Here <reference> uses the existing response-local relationship convention: exactly {"tempKey":"<same-response proofExpressions tempKey>"} or {"recordId":"<current proofExpressions canonical ID supplied by the operation>"}, with no other keys, nulls or defaults. A tempKey must resolve uniquely to a proofExpressions proposal in the same response; a recordId must resolve to the correct current family, project and scope. The APPLICATION resolves this nested relationship through the single ingestion path and at proposal acceptance replaces <reference> with the allocated/resolved canonical ID string. Agents do not write the canonical string directly. This declares the nested relationship's placement, not a second ingestion path.

Stage 06 COMPLETE or RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE may admit structurally valid tests and their availability expressions together using existing proposal acceptance. Admission and canonical ID installation do not establish proof sufficiency. Pending PROOF_REVIEW blocks readiness/evaluation as accepted availability evidence, not initial authoring or proposal admission. Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW then assesses the installed exact expression and target proposition under the existing review contract; accepted current review permits evaluation. A failed review uses the existing reconciliation/replacement/invalidation lifecycle. No user-operated reference creation is required. The expression's proposition must be availability of the exact target identified by the owning obligation's current scope; the appropriate agent proposes its semantic meaning and composition, and the application validates it.

The expression uses only the existing LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF and AT_LEAST_K language, existing valid leaf targets, evidence classes, truth extraction, accepted sufficiency review and current-scope bindings. It evaluates solely under §§29.12–29.14 and the target's existing byte/currentness/identity requirements. It must not depend on completion of the very execution whose availability it determines; ordinary acyclic prerequisite availability proof is permitted. A bare artifact record, filename, digest claim or phase label does not itself establish required byte availability. Missing, stale, unaccepted, circular or unresolved references cannot establish TRUE; apply the existing UNKNOWN/blocking rules without treating unknown as known absence. Closed-universe evidence is required to establish FALSE.

This reference does not change §16.1's due predicate or phase timing. No PHASE_TARGET, CURRENT_RECORD, VERIFIED_ARTIFACT_BYTES, or other additional condition-node grammar is introduced. An older representation may migrate only after a recorded lossless equivalence demonstration covering target, evidence, scope and TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN outcomes; otherwise affected timing/proofs remain stale pending reauthoring and review. Equivalence covers the whole effective predicate, including any separately applied phase-target constraints that the controlling source actually requires, not just the old serialized object. Existing compliant target/currentness/byte-observation functions and three-valued evaluators may be retained when their outputs are bound to the accepted existing proof contract and equivalence is demonstrated; old custom node objects are not admitted as a second canonical language. No pinned phase helper is grandfathered merely because it exists.

Each execution retains exact subject/test/fixture/target identities and hashes, selected stage and operation, current scope and history activation, actual isolation and attributable raw/native provenance. Failure validation requires an actual observation establishing rejection of the bound known-invalid fixture. Regression pre-correction failure and post-correction success require distinct executions and distinct actual target input identities; one observation cannot prove both. Existing capability, risk/disclosure authorization, human review where required, compatibility, reservation, retry, replacement, receipt, freshness and restoration controls remain mandatory and cannot be bypassed by an input-basis minimum. Supported semantic compatibility and application-observed input custody remain separate facts; a supported author interpretation does not change a valid native executor into an external one.

Role: Adversarial test designer

Visible explanation: Invalid examples are being created and checked to prove that validators catch errors.

Stage 15 — CONVERT EVERY CONFIRMED FAILURE INTO A REGRESSION TEST

Role: Change-control engineer
